text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Ruling centre-left alliance sought to keep its credibility and mend potentially fatal rifts in its ranks over plans to lead a multinational security force in Albania. Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti refuses to support the mission and shows little willingness to compromise (all).

* U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan called for the rapid deployment of the Italian-led security force in Albania, repeating that the mission was a humanitarian one rather than a military intervention (all).

* In an interview, prime minister Romano Prodi said the government does not risk a crisis even though intervention in Albania is a quite delicate matter, being Italy's first multinational mission in post-war history. Prodi invited Bertinotti to face his responsibilities and support the majority coalition (La Repubblica).

* EU Commissioner Mario Monti harshly criticised Italy's banking sector saying its inefficiency, for which both politicians and Bank of Italy are responsible, is threatening Italy's financial role and might endanger the country's future position in European Monetary Union (La Repubblica).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
